A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SceneDiff benchmark and method. Their complete main texts and appendices, including figures, equations, tables, and collection guidelines, support comparison. Revised evaluation protocols limit direct score comparisons, not document comparability.

before.justification: V1 reports original SceneDiff, RC-3D, and ChangeSim results, component ablations, robustness analyses, and a robotic demonstration.

after.justification: V2 reports original revised benchmark results, PASLCD evaluation, expanded sensitivity analyses, baseline adaptation checks, and the retained robotic demonstration.

M1.justification: The core geometry, segmentation, scoring, and association pipeline remains. Sections 4.2–4.3 change the region exclusion threshold from 60% to 50%, reduce the region-matching weight from 0.2 to 0.1, and replace accepting any sufficiently similar counterpart with one-to-one greedy matching for change classification.

E1.justification: V2 adds actual evaluation on PASLCD, previously only discussed as prior work. This extends testing to densely captured indoor and outdoor scenes under similar and different lighting conditions. SceneDiff, RC-3D, ChangeSim, and the existing dynamic-content and robotic scenarios remain.

E2.justification: SceneDiff comparisons add MV3DCD and both pretrained and fine-tuned CYWS-2D. The retained Qwen2.5-VL baseline replaces Grounding SAM localization with SAM3. RC-3D adds CYWS-2D and removes the reported VLM comparison. PASLCD comparisons additionally include SplatPose, CSCDNet, CYWS-2D, and MV3DCD, with baseline scores explicitly sourced from prior work.

E3.justification: V1 evaluates prediction centroids inside ground-truth boxes, tolerates two detections per object, and uses the highest-confidence point for scene matching. V2 introduces pixel IoU and mask-based object AP, one-to-one matching at IoU 0.5, and scene matching through aggregated IoU with mean confidence. It also adds CYWS-2D fine-tuning on 3,125 validation frame pairs and direct-box versus SAM-mask evaluation controls.

E4.justification: V2 expands sensitivity testing from change and merging thresholds to three scoring weights and four thresholds. Sections 8.6–8.7 add checks of whether SAM conversion disadvantages CYWS baselines, while Section 8.4 adds trajectory evidence explaining rendering failures. Existing dynamic-person, repetitive-object, lighting, and geometry stress analyses remain; change-type-aware evaluation is revised and relocated rather than newly introduced.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or comparable uncertainty estimates. V2's discussion of mask confidence concerns detection ranking, not statistical uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Main benchmark and ablation results are extensively revised. For SD-V, v1 reports point-based per-view/per-scene AP of 49.6/46.3, whereas v2 reports mask-based obj/im and obj/sc AP of 43.8/22.8; these are not directly comparable scores. Reported RC-3D Both AP50 changes from 68.7 to 65.3 and ChangeSim F1 from 57.6 to 57.0. New PASLCD results report 47.3 mIoU versus MV3DCD's 46.1.

T1.justification: Equations 1–6 retain their mathematical forms apart from equivalent notation and parameter retuning. Neither version adds theorems, proofs, or substantive derivations. The revised AP matching criteria are experimental protocol changes rather than new theoretical results.

C1.justification: The benchmark, training-free method, and superior-performance contributions remain. V2 explicitly elevates cross-domain generalization without retraining and improvement with advancing foundation models into abstract and conclusion claims. The reported headline relative AP margins change from 84%/37.4% to 53.0%/30.6% alongside revised comparisons.

C2.justification: V2 distinguishes geometry cues' usefulness for pixel segmentation from their weaker object-level performance, elaborates interpolation versus extrapolation as an explanation for rendering-based baseline failures, and acknowledges possible disadvantage from adapting MV3DCD. It broadens the claimed hyperparameter robustness, although Figure 19 still shows substantial change-threshold sensitivity. The principal ambiguity and reconstruction limitations remain.

D1.justification: V2 substantially expands baseline reproduction instructions, including CYWS-2D training-pair construction, MV3DCD's 60% region assignment rule, and confidence sources. It newly documents scene-consistent splits, collection effort, and using validation-selected parameters across benchmarks. V1 promises future code release; v2 states a self-contained codebase accompanies the supplement, although that attachment cannot be verified from the supplied PDFs.

R1.justification: Related work expands coverage of sensor-depth, point-cloud, and TSDF approaches, including POCD and Khronos, and adds SAM3 and SplatPose references. GPT-4 and Grounded SAM references disappear with their associated comparison changes. The central positioning around training-free object-level detection remains, with a more qualified account of rendering-based methods' strengths.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related work, experimental discussion, and conclusion undergo substantial rewriting. The benchmark section is reorganized to introduce metrics before dataset and annotation details, and the appendix structure is revised. Method explanations and terminology are also refined beyond simple renumbering.

P2.justification: V2 replaces the two-column main layout with a single-column design and substantially restructures displays. Table 2 groups methods by output type, and ablations use colored differences from the full method. New displays cover scene diversity, PASLCD, expanded sensitivity tests, trajectories, and training examples; the old point-based evaluation illustration is removed and qualitative comparison panels are revised.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially strengthens empirical validation: mask and track IoU replace permissive single-point matching, stronger baselines make comparisons more demanding, and PASLCD plus conversion and sensitivity checks address important coverage and fairness concerns. These gains outweigh the removed RC-3D VLM comparison and some overstated robustness language. The improvement comes from better evaluation and supporting evidence, not higher reported scores.
